title: The Fading Lantern Lodge Membership Crisis

scenario.title: The Fading Lantern Lodge Membership Crisis
scenario.setting: Tucked between a laundromat and a shuttered hardware store in Maplewood’s blue-collar downtown, the Fading Lantern Lodge once drew dozens of locals for weekly bingo nights and pancake breakfasts. Now its front porch only holds a single dented folding chair most days, its windows smudged with grime, and the latest membership drive netted just two new signees in three months. The only regular visitors are a handful of octogenarian members and the occasional teenager stealing shade from the summer sun.

characters.name: Marnie "Mac" MacKenzie
characters.tendencies: She rigidly prioritizes formal lodge bylaws and membership metrics, dismissing casual outreach ideas as 'unsanctioned and a waste of limited funds'

characters.name: Jazmine "Jax" Marlow
characters.tendencies: She leans into warm, nostalgic storytelling to rally locals, often sharing childhood memories of pancake breakfasts with her grandfather to convince people to join the lodge

characters.name: Burt Haggerty
characters.tendencies: He stops by the lodge occasionally for cheap coffee but hasn’t renewed his membership in three months, frustrated by the lack of new, relevant activities

characters.name: Gloria Hale
characters.tendencies: She focuses on reviving beloved old lodge events like bingo nights and holiday craft fairs, hoping to draw back former members and attract new ones through familiar, comforting activities

turns.name: Marnie "Mac" MacKenzie
turns.text:
I will not approve any unvoted community outreach initiatives. Our lodge’s operating budget is strictly allocated to hall repairs and annual charter renewal fees, not these frivolous, unsanctioned casual gatherings. Our current membership retention rate sits at just 41%, so every dollar must be accounted for per formal bylaws.
[Tapping a printed membership roster against her clipboard with sharp, deliberate taps as she brushes past a crumpled neighborhood potluck flyer stuck to the lodge’s dented screen door.]

turns.name: Jazmine "Jax" Marlow
turns.text:
Heard my grandpa’s secret blueberry pancake recipe’s headlining this Saturday’s breakfast spread at the lodge—you remember the buttery, syrupy batches we’d sneak extra blueberries for behind his old diner counter back in ‘98? C’mon on down, even if you just need a warm spot out of the crisp downtown wind and a chance to swap old stories.
[Waves a slightly coffee-stained, dog-eared flyer for the pancake breakfast over her head, grinning so wide her dimples poke through her rounded cheeks.]

turns.name: Burt Haggerty
turns.text:
Look, I just swung by for the cheap coffee—didn’t mean to start a fuss, but it’s been three months since I asked about adding a weekly carpentry workshop for folks who don’t want to knit or play bingo. Not a single thing’s changed around here, and I’m not renewing my membership until you guys quit sticking to the same old tired events.
[He shoves a crumpled one-dollar bill across the scuffed Formica counter, grabs his dented stainless steel travel mug full of lukewarm coffee, and trundles toward the exit without a backward glance.]

turns.name: Gloria Hale
turns.text:
Hey neighbor, we’re finally getting our old bingo night back up and running this Saturday afternoon! It’s free to join, we’ve got homemade apple cider and peanut brittle for everyone, and the grand prize is a jar of my mom’s preserved blackberry jam. We’re also collecting gently used winter hats and gloves for the local elementary school’s cozy closet while you’re here.
[Straightening a stack of neon bingo cards on the lodge’s scuffed wooden front counter and tapping a hand-drawn “Bingo This Saturday!” sign into place beside the warped screen door.]

turns.name: Marnie "Mac" MacKenzie
turns.text:
I won’t entertain these unsanctioned, last-minute community offerings—they siphon away our limited operating funds that are meant strictly for hall repairs and charter compliance. Burt, your carpentry works request requires a full membership vote per our official bylaws, not a casual drop-in pitch, and Jax and Gloria’s event plans need to go through the proper approval channels first. I’m not diverting any budget dollars to subsidize pancake spreads or bingo nights right now.
[Taps a dog-eared copy of the lodge’s official bylaws against her clipboard, jaw set tightly]

turns.name: Jazmine "Jax" Marlow
turns.text:
C’mon, Mac—Burt’s been bugging me nonstop about his carpentry spot for three months, and my grandpa’s blueberry pancakes are the perfect way to drag every last neighbor through the lodge doors. We can slot a quick test run of his drop-in hour right after the breakfast line wraps, and Gloria’s already lined up homemade apple cider for bingo anyway, so folks will stick around for hours after that.
[leans in with a soft, playful grin and flutters a crumpled stack of handwritten pancake breakfast sign-up sheets from her worn flannel hip pocket]

turns.name: Burt Haggerty
turns.text:
I saw the bingo notice taped to the laundromat’s bulletin board, and that’s nice for the regulars, but I didn’t trek over here just for a free apple cider. That carpentry workshop I asked about three months back hasn’t gotten so much as a quick reply from the lodge board. I just wanted to offer a low-key space for folks who like fixing things, whether that’s their own porch railings or neighborhood park birdhouses.
[He sets his half-empty, chipped ceramic coffee mug down with a soft clink on the scuffed front counter, crossing his arms over his worn flannel shirt.]

turns.name: Gloria Hale
turns.text:
I also put together a donated prize basket stuffed with local wildflower honey and hand-knit scarves for the bingo night’s top winner, and we’ve got free neon bingo daubers for anyone who forgets their own. It’ll feel just like the cozy, familiar bingo nights we all loved back when the lodge was humming with weekly gatherings.
[I tap a stack of brightly colored bingo cards against the scuffed front wooden counter and nod toward the steaming crockpot of spiced apple cider sitting on a folding table by the door.]

dm_opening: DM opening: the Marnie "Mac" MacKenzie takes a position; the cast gathers around a question the scene has been carrying for a year.
dm_closing: DM closing: the Marnie "Mac" MacKenzie still holds the line; the next session's hook — a new member, an old scar — is already at the door.
